prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, showing how exporting and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade and making trade models testable on firm-level data.

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I preferred B015 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) and listed B038 as my first alternative, describing the two as close in strength. After the exchange I now prefer B038. I apply one standard to every candidate: a specific, identifiable scientific contribution, an explanatory framework tied to data, maturity of the evidence, and a credit set the committee can defend. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extensions changed the unit of analysis in trade from industries to firms. They gave a mechanism for exporter selection and within-industry reallocation, and a productivity channel for the gains from trade. That mechanism has been taken to customs and production microdata for more than twenty years, and it has been used in macro, industrial organisation and development. This is the pairing of an explanatory framework with micro-level data that I value most. Two things in the exchange moved me. First, Friberg separated the persistence of a workhorse framework from confirmation of specific credited building blocks, and noted that the micro evidence on time-dependent versus state-dependent pricing is mixed. That weakens the case for crediting Calvo's pricing rule as an established finding, as opposed to a tractable device that was extremely useful. Second, Enflo and Boppart clarified that the 2008 trade prize concerned scale economies, product differentiation and the location of production, and that firm-level selection is a later, separately testable step. I treat the 2008 trade prize and the earlier macroeconomics prizes on expectations, time consistency and policy rules symmetrically. Each narrows the incremental contribution without disqualifying either candidate. The citation I propose is built around the selection and reallocation mechanism, not around the size of welfare gains. The mechanism is much better supported than any single magnitude. I do not use support counts as merit. B015 remains a first-rank scientific contribution and my first alternative. My move reflects attribution and the weaker credit case for Calvo's pricing, not a lower view of the framework's influence.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have serious claims on the closely related firm-level trade literature and the exporter facts, and none of them is in the credited names. A Melitz-Helpman award could be read as under-crediting them. The 2008 prize narrows the incremental step, and the committee has to decide whether firm-level selection is a distinct discovery. Gains-from-trade magnitudes depend on elasticity and functional-form assumptions, which is comparable in kind to the framework dependence I raised against B015. Helpman's appearance on B030 means his credit has to be accounted for once, though I see it as separable from the selection work. If the committee finds that the B015 attribution can be settled around a clear origin-plus-synthesis citation, B015 remains a defensible first choice. B015's post-2021 inflation and heterogeneous-agent questions are better treated as limits on the simple model than as refutation of nominal rigidity.

responses.point: Friberg argues that a framework's survival through 2008 and 2021-23 shows usefulness and adaptability, not confirmation of the specific credited building blocks. He also cautions that Calvo pricing is a tractable device and that micro evidence on price adjustment is mixed.
responses.response: This moved me. I had treated survival through the post-2008 and post-2021 episodes as support for the credited trio. Your distinction shows that this supports the framework more than it supports the claim that Calvo pricing was an established finding. It makes a B015 citation harder to write with Calvo in it. I still think Taylor's contracts and rule and Woodford's synthesis have a stronger claim, but a trio built around the framework's origins loses force once the pricing rule is read as a device. That is one reason I now prefer the cleaner B038 set. I would apply your standard to B038 too. The firm-level exporter facts predated the model, so the confirming evidence is for selection and reallocation, not for particular welfare numbers.

responses.point: Enflo reads the 2008 prize as covering scale economies, product differentiation and the location of production, not firm-level selection. She therefore treats B038 as a successor and not a duplicate. She also words the citation around the mechanism and not the size of the gains.
responses.response: I accept that distinction, and it addresses part of my own round-1 concern. I would add that the committee should apply the same overlap test to B015 and not only to B038. Earlier macroeconomics prizes on expectations, time consistency and policy rules narrow B015's incremental step in a way parallel to the 2008 prize. I do not think either overlap is disqualifying. I do not fully resolve the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum question, which you list among your own uncertainties. I handle it by agreeing that the citation should name the theoretical selection model and its welfare implications and should not claim the whole empirical firm-trade literature.

responses.point: Hassler replied to my round-1 point that the heterogeneous-agent critique and the 2021-23 inflation are an extension and partial challenge, not a refutation of nominal rigidity. He wants a citation worded around foundations and not current empirical performance.
responses.response: I accept your reading and have changed my view of how much those episodes should count against B015. They test the Phillips-curve specification and the shocks, and they do not overturn the case for nominal rigidity. My move to B038 does not rest on them. It rests on attribution and on the chair-summary question about which building blocks the evidence confirms. You prefer Calvo and Taylor to Galí and Gertler because they are origins. I find that principled, and I would not object to your trio as a B015 outcome. But the estimation contributions of Christiano-Eichenbaum, Smets and Galí have no home in it, and Friberg's point on Calvo makes the origin claim harder to state. B038 does not have that problem to the same degree.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize for its clean attribution to one 1997 paper, and concedes that direct empirical identification of the collateral-amplification channel is mixed.
responses.response: I weigh the clean attribution seriously, and it is an advantage of B050 over B015. It is also the advantage that now counts for B038. I still do not place B050 in my alternatives. Your own caveat, and Dreber's, that post-2008 evidence shows financial frictions matter without validating this specific channel leaves the empirical side thinner than B038's. The chair asked what direct evidence targets the collateral-constraint channel itself. Neither of you has given one in round 1, and I am open to being shown it. If it exists, I would move B050 up as an alternative.

responses.point: Boppart argues that the citation should describe the firm-selection model and its welfare implications, not the whole firm-level trade literature. He treats Redding's quantitative and spatial work as a later extension, not the founding contribution.
responses.response: I agree on both, and this is why I keep the set at two names. In round 1 I said the Melitz-Helpman pairing was less clean than it looked because of Bernard and others. Your wording answers that: limit the claim to the theoretical selection model, and the narrower credit becomes defensible without implying that others' work is lesser. I would not add Redding. I would leave the third place empty and not widen the citation toward quantitative trade.

uncertainties: Whether Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have claims strong enough that a two-name Melitz-Helpman prize would look incomplete, and whether wording the citation around the theoretical selection model is enough.
How much the 2008 trade prize, and earlier macroeconomics prizes for B015, should narrow the incremental case. I apply the same test to both and do not claim it is settled.
How robust the gains-from-trade magnitudes are to elasticity and functional-form assumptions, and whether the qualitative selection and reallocation result is the right object to cite.
Whether the B015 attribution could be settled around a defensible trio, and in that case whether it should rank above B038. I treat that as the main way I could revert.
How to account for Helpman's credit on B030 once, if the committee proceeds with B038.
My assessments rest on general knowledge of the literature and the supplied materials, and I have not independently verified citation or credit records.
statement.conflict_note: Updated: none apparent from the supplied profile. My listed frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) do not appear among the credited names on B038, B015 or B036, and I have no listed tie to Melitz, Helpman, Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. My research field, labour economics and crime, is adjacent to B036, an alternative, and I treat that as field proximity, not a personal connection. I have no listed tie to the members who prefer other parts, and I have weighed their arguments as evidence only. I have not adjudicated any disclosed tie.
